records.source: Google Search Central, SEO Starter Guide
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: The search engine itself names most of the folk SEO surface as inert: keywords meta tag unused, no word-count target, heading order irrelevant to ranking, keywords in the domain or URL near worthless, and E-E-A-T explicitly not a ranking factor. What it does claim to weigh is content people find useful, crawlability and discovery through links. The decision rule that follows is to spend the budget on the small set of things the operator of the index says it reads, and to treat every other lever as a preference an agent must not assert as law.
records.applicability_limits: One vendor describing its own closed ranking system with no external verification, and the doc gives no weights or thresholds, so it settles what is not worth doing far better than it settles what is. Says nothing about Bing, AI assistants that do not use Google's index, or any non-search channel.
records.counter_evidence: The SEO trade press routinely reports ranking correlations that contradict Google's public denials; none of that reporting is a controlled experiment either, so the disagreement is unresolved rather than settled in Google's favour.
records.review: on-change-of:Google Search Central SEO Starter Guide revision date

records.source: Google Search Central, Spam policies for Google web search
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: Sixteen named policies, of which three bite directly on agent-assisted marketing: scaled content abuse (many pages generated mainly to move rankings rather than help a reader), site reputation abuse (renting an established domain's ranking signals to third-party content) and expired domain abuse. The policy hinges on purpose rather than production method, so the binding rule for an agent estate is a per-page purpose test and a human-attributable owner, not a cap on how much the machine writes.
records.applicability_limits: Enforcement is discretionary and opaque, with no published detection thresholds, so the policy states a boundary without letting anyone measure their distance from it. Written for web search, not for AI answer surfaces or other engines.
records.review: on-change-of:Google Search spam policies revision date

records.source: Google Search Central, General structured data guidelines
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: Markup must describe what a reader can actually see on the page, marked-up pages must not be blocked from the crawler, and the penalty for breach is loss of rich-result eligibility rather than a ranking drop. That gives a clean machine-checkable contract: every marked-up property has a visible counterpart in the rendered DOM, and the blast radius of getting it wrong is bounded and known in advance.
records.applicability_limits: Governs eligibility for Google's rich results only. Says nothing about whether any rich result is worth having, and the required and recommended property sets differ per feature type, so a generic validator is not enough.
records.review: on-change-of:Google general structured data guidelines revision date

records.source: Google Search Central, Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: The guidance is a self-assessment questionnaire organised as who wrote it, how it was made and why it exists, and it asks that substantial automation including AI generation be self-evident to the visitor. It does not ban machine-written content; it asks for disclosed provenance and a purpose other than ranking. For an agent estate that converts neatly into a per-artefact provenance record.
records.applicability_limits: A questionnaire, not a scoring rubric: two honest people can answer the same way about pages of very different quality, and none of it is externally auditable. The stricter Your Money or Your Life framing is asserted without published criteria.
records.review: on-change-of:Google helpful content guidance revision date

records.source: Google Search Central, Optimising your website for AI features on Google Search
records.licence: CC BY 4.0 for page content, Apache-2.0 for code samples
records.finding: Google states there are no additional requirements or special optimisations for AI Overviews and AI Mode, and specifically that no new machine-readable file, AI text file or markup is needed. Eligibility is ordinary indexing plus snippet eligibility. The binding consequence is that a pack must not let an agent invent a generative-engine-optimisation workstream on the strength of vendor-adjacent hype.
records.applicability_limits: Covers Google's surfaces only. Other assistants crawl and cite differently, and some publishers do serve llms.txt for non-Google consumers, so the claim is narrow rather than universal. Google has a commercial interest in discouraging parallel optimisation channels, so this is a self-interested denial, not neutral evidence.
records.counter_evidence: The llms.txt proposal and its adopters constitute a live counter-practice, unvalidated by any measurement this research could find.
records.review: on-change-of:Google AI features guidance revision date

records.licence: IETF Trust Legal Provisions (BSD-style licence on code components); text reproducible under RFC terms
records.finding: Crawler access rules are advisory only: the RFC states plainly that the protocol is not a substitute for content security measures. It also fixes the failure semantics that matter operationally, a 5xx on robots.txt means the crawler must assume complete disallow, and cached rules should not be used beyond twenty four hours. So a botched robots.txt deploy is a self-inflicted deindexing incident, which makes robots.txt a release-gated artefact rather than a marketing file.
records.applicability_limits: Compliance is voluntary; hostile scrapers ignore it entirely. The RFC governs crawling, not indexing, so a disallowed URL can still surface from external links.

records.source: RFC 8058, Signalling One-Click Functionality for List Email Headers
records.licence: IETF Trust Legal Provisions (BSD-style licence on code components); text reproducible under RFC terms
records.finding: One-click unsubscribe is a hard technical contract, not a courtesy: an HTTPS List-Unsubscribe URI plus List-Unsubscribe-Post, both covered by the DKIM signature, recipient and list identity encoded in the URI, no cookies or HTTP authorisation, and no confirmation page. The URI should carry an opaque hard-to-forge component that the server validates, which is what stops the unsubscribe endpoint becoming an open denial-of-subscription hole.
records.applicability_limits: Specifies the signalling mechanism only. It does not say how fast the suppression must take effect, does not cover consent capture, and does not reach any channel other than mail.

records.source: Google Workspace Admin Help, Email sender guidelines
records.version_or_commit: requirements effective 2024-02-01, page as accessed 2026-08-03; no explicit revision id published
records.finding: Deliverability has a published numeric gate. Every sender needs SPF or DKIM, valid forward and reverse DNS, TLS, RFC 5322 conformance and a Postmaster Tools spam rate under 0.30 per cent. Bulk senders above five thousand messages a day additionally need SPF and DKIM and DMARC, From-header alignment with the SPF or DKIM domain, and RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe with a visible in-body link. That converts a soft craft into a preflight checklist a machine can assert before a first send.
records.applicability_limits: Gmail's rules for Gmail. Yahoo and Microsoft publish overlapping but not identical thresholds, and reporting at this cutoff says Yahoo computes the spam-rate denominator differently, from inbox-delivered mail rather than all delivered mail, so a single number cannot be treated as universal. The spam-rate figure is only observable through Google's own Postmaster Tools, which requires DKIM-signed volume to populate.

records.source: Privacy and Electronic Communications (EC Directive) Regulations 2003, regulation 22
records.version_or_commit: SI 2003/2426 reg 22, as amended; text showing amendments in force to 2026-02-05 including the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 charity exception at paragraph 3A
records.finding: Unsolicited marketing mail to an individual subscriber requires prior consent, with one narrow escape: the soft opt-in, which needs all three of contact details obtained in the course of a sale or sales negotiation with that person, marketing of similar products and services only, and a simple free refusal route offered both at collection and in every subsequent message. The provenance of every address is therefore a compliance fact that must be stored with the address, not inferred later.
records.applicability_limits: UK law, and the regulation covers electronic mail to subscribers; the individual versus corporate subscriber distinction and the enforcement practice sit in ICO guidance rather than in the regulation text. EU member states implement the parent directive with local variation, and US CAN-SPAM is an opt-out regime entirely, so a single global consent rule is wrong in one direction or the other.

records.source: Gordon, Zettelmeyer, Bhargava and Chapsky, A Comparison of Approaches to Advertising Measurement: Evidence from Big Field Experiments at Facebook
records.study_design: Fifteen large-scale randomised advertising experiments used as ground truth, against which several observational estimators (exposed versus unexposed comparison, regression, propensity and matching methods) are re-estimated on the same data
records.population: Facebook advertisers in the United States; approximately 500 million user-experiment observations and 1.6 billion ad impressions
records.version_or_commit: Marketing Science vol 38 no 2, pages 193 to 225, published March 2019
records.licence: unknown (INFORMS subscription content; abstract publicly readable)
records.finding: With individual-level data far richer than any small venture will ever hold, observational estimates of advertising effect still failed to reproduce the randomised estimates, even after conditioning on extensive demographic and behavioural variables. The authors conclude the industry's usual data does not contain the exogenous variation needed. The decision rule is that any causal claim about a channel must come from a randomised holdout, and dashboard attribution is at best a bookkeeping convention.
records.applicability_limits: One platform, one era, mostly large advertisers with big budgets and small percentage effects; it does not follow that observational methods fail equally in every setting, and the paper does not tell a two-person venture what to do when a holdout is unaffordable. Access here was the public abstract and record page rather than the full text.
records.counter_evidence: Later work in the same journal, Close Enough? (Marketing Science 2023), explores non-experimental approaches more sympathetically, so the field's position is a spectrum rather than a flat prohibition.

records.source: Lewis, Zettelmeyer, Gordon et al, Amazon Ads Multi-Touch Attribution
records.study_design: Methodology paper describing an attribution system that calibrates machine-learned observational credit allocation against randomised controlled trials
records.finding: The stated trade-off is explicit: observational models scale and are precise but can be biased, randomised trials are unbiased but noisy, so credit allocation is anchored to experimental estimates and the model only distributes within that anchor. The transferable rule is that an attribution model is a way of spreading an experimentally measured total, never a way of producing one.
records.applicability_limits: A preprint by the platform about its own product, not independently replicated, and it needs a continuous RCT programme at a scale no small venture has. It is evidence for the architecture of the argument rather than for the numbers.
records.review: on-change-of:arXiv 2508.08209 new version or journal publication

records.source: Google Analytics Help, Attribution and attribution modelling in Google Analytics 4
records.version_or_commit: page as accessed 2026-08-03; documents the November 2023 model removal
records.finding: The dominant analytics vendor deleted first-click, linear, time-decay and position-based attribution from its own product in November 2023, leaving data-driven attribution and two last-click variants, and it excludes direct visits from credit unless the whole path is direct. That is a vendor conceding that heuristic credit-splitting rules were arbitrary. A pack should therefore treat any percentage split across touchpoints as a reporting convention to be declared, never as a measured quantity.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor documentation of a proprietary model whose internals are not published and cannot be audited or reproduced. Coverage degrades where consent is refused or cross-device identity is unavailable, and the doc does not quantify that gap.

records.source: Reforge, Growth Loops are the New Funnels (Balfour, Winters, Kwok, Chen)
records.version_or_commit: unknown; essay series first circulated July 2018, no revision id published
records.finding: The argued case against funnels is organisational as much as mathematical: a funnel splits strategy and ownership by stage, so marketing optimises acquisition and product optimises retention against each other, and growth stays linear because output never re-enters input. A loop is a closed system whose output is reinvested as input. The usable rule is to require a named reinvestment step in any growth plan, and to treat a plan with no reinvestment step as a paid-acquisition budget rather than a growth strategy.
records.applicability_limits: Practitioner essay with no data, no measurement and no falsifiable claim; a consultancy's positioning artefact for its own curriculum. Direct access was refused with HTTP 403 at this cutoff, so the content here rests on the authors' own public thread and secondary summaries rather than the page itself, and the argument should be marked down accordingly.
records.counter_evidence: Nothing in the loop argument is inconsistent with funnel analytics as a diagnostic; the essay overstates the opposition, and tools such as PostHog (FRAG-MKTG-15) continue to ship funnels because step-level drop-off is still the cheapest diagnostic available.
records.review: on-change-of:direct access to the Reforge essay becoming possible

records.version_or_commit: unknown; living page, no revision id published
records.finding: A developer-tools company publishes its marketing operating rules in the open and reduces them to three: be opinionated, pull rather than push, and no sneaky shit. Marketing is organised as six small cross-functional teams (graphics, website, marketing, editorial, video, docs) rather than a channel hierarchy. The transferable move is that a small marketing function is a set of publishing teams with a stated stance, and the stance is what makes agent-generated content non-generic.
records.applicability_limits: Self-description by a venture-funded company selling to developers, with no reported outcome data attached to the principles, so it is a plausible exemplar rather than evidence that the approach works. Pull-not-push depends on having a technical audience that reads; it transfers badly to categories with no organic reading habit. The page is a live document with no version marker, so any citation dates immediately.
records.counter_evidence: The brand-building evidence tradition (FRAG-MKTG-16) argues that pull-only strategies underinvest in the mental availability that reaches non-searching buyers.

records.version_or_commit: unknown; living docs page, no revision id published
records.finding: A funnel is only defined once its parameters are declared: sequential versus strict-order versus any-order steps, exclusion steps that remove people from the whole funnel, and conversion measured either against the first step or against the previous step. Two teams quoting different conversion rates for the same product are usually quoting different parameter sets. So the pack should require the funnel definition to be stored as configuration next to the number, and any reported rate without it to be rejected.
records.applicability_limits: Vendor product documentation, and the page carries no warning against reading step drop-off as causal, which is the mistake most funnel reporting actually makes. Conversion-window semantics were not visible in the section retrieved, so that parameter remains unverified here.

records.source: Ehrenberg-Bass Institute for Marketing Science, Effective brand growth: acquisition or retention
records.study_design: Institute summary of longitudinal panel analyses of brand share change, resting on the double jeopardy empirical generalisation and citing Riebe, Wright, Stern and Sharp (2014) on service-category brands
records.population: Repeat-purchase consumer and service categories across many countries and decades
records.version_or_commit: undated institute page, timestamped roughly 2019 at access
records.licence: Copyright Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, all rights reserved; paraphrase only
records.finding: Share growth comes overwhelmingly from acquiring category buyers rather than from reducing defection, and the institute puts acquisition at roughly twice the importance of retention. Under double jeopardy, small brands have both fewer buyers and slightly lower loyalty, and loyalty is largely a function of size rather than a lever that produces it. The decision rule is that a retention-first growth plan for a small brand is almost certainly the wrong plan, and reach to non-buyers is the default.
records.applicability_limits: The empirical base is repeat-purchase consumer goods and mass-market services, with large sample sizes but light-touch category coverage of B2B software, high-consideration purchases and subscription products where negative churn is a real mechanism. This is an institute summary rather than the underlying papers, all-rights-reserved so paraphrase only, and the institute has a commercial interest in the conclusion.
records.counter_evidence: Product-led and loop-based growth thinking (FRAG-MKTG-13) treats existing-user behaviour as the primary engine of new-user acquisition, which is not the same claim as retention-first but does put weight where Ehrenberg-Bass takes it away.

records.source: Binet and Field, The Long and the Short of It (IPA)
records.study_design: Analysis of the IPA Effectiveness Awards Databank, reported as 996 campaigns across roughly 700 brands and 83 sectors over three decades of submitted case studies
records.population: Mostly UK advertisers large enough to enter effectiveness awards
records.licence: unknown; IPA and WARC content is paywalled
records.finding: Brand-building and sales activation behave differently in time: activation produces a sharp short-lived lift, brand-building a slower compounding one, and the reported optimum split is around sixty per cent brand to forty per cent activation. The transferable principle is that a marketing plan must declare a time horizon per activity, because a single blended ROI number will always select activation and quietly starve the compounding half.
records.applicability_limits: An industry effectiveness report, recorded as blog because the enum has no value for it and the primary text could not be read. The primary text and the WARC commentary were both paywalled at this cutoff, so this record rests on secondary reporting and should be treated as a directional claim, not a verified one. The databank is self-selected award entries, which is a survivorship-biased sample; the 60:40 figure is an average across categories that the authors themselves have since qualified by category and business model, and it was derived in a pre-digital-dominant media landscape.
records.counter_evidence: The randomised-measurement literature (FRAG-MKTG-10) implies that the ROI figures underlying award case studies are themselves observational and likely biased, which weakens the arithmetic behind any specific split.
records.review: on-change-of:access to the IPA primary text
